title: Wagon cup holder: v2, hanging off the side rail
subtitle: Bolt-tightened clip on the right-hand side rail · hangs a 20 oz Yeti off the outside of the wagon · shown in print orientation · millimetres
scale_note: Real size. The rail is your 22.3 mm tube (assumed the same on the side rail). The tumbler is from retailer listings (70 mm base, 89 mm widest), not your cup. It is drawn in print orientation: the clip's rail axis is vertical here and the cup lies on its side. In use the rail is horizontal and the cup stands upright, hanging off the outside of it.
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v2: you wanted the cup hanging off the side of the wagon, and your photos show the right-hand side rail is the place for that. The clip wraps the rail with its mouth facing down; a shelf and a web carry the cup out 68 mm and down 60 mm to a pocket beside the frame. The cup now twists the clip all the time (about 0.7 N·m full), so the M4 x 35 bolt across the clip's ears is essential. You reach its head with a hex key through the window in the web, from inside the empty pocket, so tighten it before the cup goes in. Please check: (1) is the side rail the same 22.3 mm tube? (2) is the red latch or the diagonal strut outboard of the rail in the 70 mm clip zone? If so the web will hit it. (3) is the clip the right spot, not further toward the end cap? (4) measure your tumbler's base and widest diameter. Print the 15 mm clip test slice first.
